payload.body: Cutpurses work market crowds of lowland trade towns where coin moves faster than watchful eyes. They were raised in lean years after the imperial fall, when a full purse mattered more than honest trade. Most carry a short knife less for killing than for cutting strings and frightening victims still. Ordinary folk fear the slow bleed of lost wages more than wounds, while merchants beat caught thieves bloody. The town watch punishes them with whipping and branding rather than hanging, yet scarred veterans return quickly. They run in loose pairs, one to jostle and one to lift, scattering quickly once steel is drawn. In open combat a cornered cutpurse fights wild and low, aiming to wound a leg and escape through alleys. Travelers sew coin inside sleeves and never chase a thief alone through darkening streets at dusk. Every escape teaches the watch new patience, and every branding only sharpens a cutpurse's careful timing.
payload.base_appearance: A wiry hooded figure slips through crowds in a patched cloak, shoulders hunched and movements deliberately unremarkable. A short palmed knife hides along one forearm, complemented by slashed pockets and a cord for lifted purses. Lean limbs and quick fingers complete the silhouette, built for sudden sprints down narrow rain-slick alleys.
payload.portrait_brief: A narrow youthful face watches sideways beneath a pulled hood, with close-cropped hair and a faded scar. Quick suspicious eyes and a tight mouth convey hunger, cunning, and constant readiness to bolt.

variants.name: Young Cutpurse
variants.appearance_delta: A lean boyish build with a too-large cloak and freshly nicked fingers from recent practice.

variants.name: Elder Cutpurse
variants.appearance_delta: A gaunt older man with branded cheeks, grey stubble, and a knife worn smooth by decades.

variants.name: Cutpurse Girl
variants.appearance_delta: A small quick girl with bound hair, ragged shawl, and coins stitched secretly inside her cuffs.

variants.name: Shawl Woman
variants.appearance_delta: A weary woman in a heavy shawl whose broad skirts conceal slashed linings and hidden pockets.

state_poses.description: He sidles through the crowd with shoulders low, one hand hovering near a stranger's purse strings.
He lunges forward with a low slashing cut aimed at purse cords or an exposed leg.
He doubles over clutching his ribs, coins scattering across the cobbles as he staggers backward.
He lies sprawled face-down with scattered coins glittering around his outstretched fingers.

payload.body: Burglars break timber houses and store-rooms of forest and highland towns where walls yield to a quiet pry-bar. They know shutters and patrol-change hours, lore passed patiently from cellmate to cellmate since tired garrisons thinned. They avoid faces whenever possible, preferring empty rooms and silent drawers to drawn blades and shouting. Households dread the morning discovery most, for stolen tools and winter stores take seasons to replace. Courts hang repeat house-breakers without mercy, so scarred elders carry rope-burns from narrowly escaped arrests. In open fight they swing crowbar and hammer with workman strength but no drill, dangerous only when trapped. They surrender quickly once outnumbered and surrounded, having learned that living thieves steal again another night. Valley farms keep geese, barred doors, and sleepless dogs, trusting noise more than locks against quiet intruders. Every captured burglar teaches neighbors new precautions, yet empty houses always tempt the next desperate night crew.
payload.base_appearance: A dark-wool laborer moves quietly in soot-smudged clothes, with a pry-bar slung low and a sack across the back. Sturdy boots, fingerless gloves, and a coiled rope complete the working kit of a patient house-breaker. Watchful narrowed eyes and a hunched carriage suggest someone accustomed to windows, ledges, and midnight timber.
payload.portrait_brief: A plain weathered face peers from beneath a wool cap, with soot-smudged cheeks and cautious narrowed eyes. Thin lips and a strong jaw convey patience, while small ears listen constantly for patrols and dogs.

variants.name: Climber Burglar
variants.appearance_delta: A wiry young man with rope-burned palms, soft boots, and plaster dust whitening his dark sleeves.

variants.name: Breaker Burglar
variants.appearance_delta: A broad older man with a heavy pry-bar, scarred knuckles, and shoulders built for forcing shutters.

variants.name: Lockpick Burglar
variants.appearance_delta: A deft woman with slender picks in her cuffs, oiled hair, and patient practiced fingertips.

variants.name: Carrier Burglar
variants.appearance_delta: A sturdy woman with an oversized sack, padded shoulders, and quiet shoes for laden escapes.

state_poses.description: He crouches beside a shuttered window with pry-bar raised, listening for footsteps before forcing entry.
He swings the crowbar overhead in a heavy arc meant to break guards and doorframes alike.
He staggers sideways clutching his shoulder, the sack slipping as barred doors slam around him.
He lies face-down across his spilled sack with tools scattered uselessly around his hands.

payload.body: Smugglers move untaxed salt and iron along delta channels and marsh causeways where checkpoints miss every reed. They fattened after the imperial fracture made every border a toll, turning honest boatmen into patient outlaws. Boatmen and carters first and knife-fighters second, they know every ford that marching soldiers forget. Common folk both quietly use and openly resent them, glad for cheap goods yet angry when harvests lose value. Patrols seize boats more often than lives, leaving heavy debts that drive crews straight back to the water. Cornered they fight back-to-back with hooks and cudgels, tougher than cutpurses from hauling wet cargo. They rarely murder hungry travelers outright, for fresh bodies draw soldiers and close profitable channels for seasons. Their names change in every river port, and no manifest they carry has ever borne the truth. Burned boats teach caution for a season, but hunger and debt always launch new hulls before spring floods.
payload.base_appearance: An oilskin waterman stands sure-footed in tar-stained canvas, with a hook-pole balanced across one shoulder. Rope belts, patched waders, and a short heavy cudgel complete the working dress of delta channels. Weather-beaten skin and narrowed river eyes suggest someone who reads currents better than written laws.
payload.portrait_brief: A broad wind-burned face grins beneath a tarred hat, with wet hair plastered across the forehead. Sharp watchful eyes and a crooked nose convey permanent suspicion of uniforms, tolls, and strangers.

variants.name: Boatsman Smuggler
variants.appearance_delta: A lean young man with rope-calloused hands, bare feet, and a pole worn smooth by currents.

variants.name: Carter Smuggler
variants.appearance_delta: A heavy older man with a salt-stained coat, whip at his belt, and false cart bottoms.

variants.name: River Girl
variants.appearance_delta: A quick young woman with braided hair, rolled sleeves, and hidden pouches sewn inside her skirts.

variants.name: Ferry Widow
variants.appearance_delta: An older widow in oilskin and shawl whose quiet ferry carries more than lawful passengers.

state_poses.description: He stands balanced aboard a rocking skiff with hook-pole grounded, watching both banks for patrols.
He hauls on the hook-pole with a wrenching pull meant to drag foes into black water.
He reels sideways with one foot slipping, arms windmilling above the gunwale as cargo shifts.
He kneels sunk in shallow water beside his leaking boat, hands raised in surrender.

payload.body: Counterfeiters file and wash coins in hidden back rooms of market towns, stretching scarce silver thinner with each successor mint. Their crime needs no blade until discovered, when the penalty waiting at the gallows is the noose. Often failed smiths or dismissed clerks, they learned honest weights in old shops before imperial pay finally stopped. Merchants fear them worst of all thieves, for one bad coin quietly poisons every later trade. Informers earn generous rewards, so careful frightened masters trust no apprentice long and move presses by night. In combat they are weakest of this criminal kin, flailing hammer and tongs in open panic. They keep hired muscle when rich enough, else bargain and beg desperately before ever swinging a tool. Villagers test every coin with their teeth now, biting silver because these forgers taught them suspicion. Each seized press closes one cellar, yet debt and clever fingers always open another before the spring snows melt.
payload.base_appearance: A scorched-apron artisan hunches over hidden work, with burnt fingers, stained cuffs, and darting nervous eyes. Files, scales, and small hammers fill the belt, beneath a coat dusted with pale metal shavings. A stooped posture and ink-darkened nails betray long nights spent weighing false silver by candlelight.
payload.portrait_brief: A pale anxious face sweats beneath thinning hair, with burnt eyebrows and eyes that never rest. A twitching mouth and bitten lip convey constant fear of informers, inspectors, and the gallows.

variants.name: Filer Counterfeiter
variants.appearance_delta: A thin young man with scarred fingertips, magnifier at his belt, and sleeves grey with filings.

variants.name: Master Counterfeiter
variants.appearance_delta: An older artisan with calm hands, hidden scales, and a press concealed beneath floorboards.

variants.name: Clerk Counterfeiter
variants.appearance_delta: A neat young woman with ink-stained cuffs, false ledgers, and weights sewn into her hem.

variants.name: Washer Counterfeiter
variants.appearance_delta: An older woman with acid-pale hands, aprons layered against stains, and vats behind locked doors.

state_poses.description: He cringes behind his workbench with hammer raised, eyes flicking toward every door and window.
He flails wildly with hammer and tongs, swinging in panicked arcs that barely threaten trained foes.
He covers his face with both arms as struck tools clatter across the workshop floor.
He lies slumped across scattered false coins with his press overturned and furnace cold.

payload.body: Fences buy stolen goods in locked shops behind chandleries and pawn-stalls of busy trade and timber towns. They never lift purses themselves, yet they patiently make theft profitable, so honest watches hate them most. Many began as honest brokers when roads ran safely, then learned that unasked questions earn quiet silver. Common folk pawn honest heirloom goods beside stolen ones unknowing, while ciphered ledgers hide every guilty transaction. Courts patiently fine them ruinously to seize hidden stock, preferring bankruptcy over the trouble of a hanging. A cornered fence fights like a desperate shopkeeper, swinging a cudgel while shouting loudly for the watch. He pays blood-money on the spot rather than trading prolonged blows, valuing intact stock above pride. Loyal shop-boys with heavy staves sometimes stand beside him, answering wages rather than any written law. Each raided shop teaches harder lessons in concealment, and fresh ciphers reopen quiet trade before the season turns.
payload.base_appearance: A heavy-coated shopkeeper stands planted among crowded shelves, with jeweled rings, a ledger pouch, and a stout cudgel. Keys, tallies, and ciphered tags crowd the belt, beneath a fur-trimmed coat that suggests comfortable profits. A calculating smile and folded arms complete the picture of a merchant who never asks origins.
payload.portrait_brief: A round bargaining face beams beneath oiled hair, with small bright eyes that weigh every visitor. A neat beard and heavy jowls convey prosperity, patience, and quiet knowledge of guilty stock.

variants.name: Young Fence
variants.appearance_delta: A slick young broker with fresh rings, polished scales, and a back room already full.

variants.name: Elder Fence
variants.appearance_delta: A grey older dealer with cipher books, trembling hands, and decades of unasked questions.

variants.name: Widow Fence
variants.appearance_delta: A composed widow in dark silks whose pawn-stall quietly absorbs the town's stolen silver.

variants.name: Clerk Fence
variants.appearance_delta: A sharp young woman with tally boards, quick arithmetic, and ledgers written in careful code.

state_poses.description: He stands with arms spread wide among his wares, smiling as though every customer were honest.
He chops downward with his cudgel in short shopkeeper swings aimed at arms and shoulders.
He clutches his ribs and staggers backward into stacked shelves as pottery crashes around him.
He sits slumped among scattered wares with his ledger torn and strongbox hanging open.

payload.body: Lookouts serve as the sharp eyes of street gangs in crowded market and dock quarters where alleys turn fast. Mostly hungry desperate youths paid in stolen scraps, they whistle clear warning signals and scatter quickly at the first approaching helm. They know every rooftop gap and narrow cellar door from childhood games that slowly turned into work. Ordinary busy folk ignore them as stray children, until a sudden robbery follows their innocent signal. Watches rarely hang such young street thieves, settling for beatings that harden them into full members. In a fight they are weakest of the gang, throwing stones and knives from distance before fleeing. Cornered they drop their blades and beg shamelessly for mercy, having watched what happens to those who resist. Their sudden unexplained absence from a familiar street warns seasoned travelers more than their watching presence. Each beating graduates another lookout into muscle, and younger siblings always wait to take the empty corner.
payload.base_appearance: A ragged barefoot youth darts between corners, with a sling at the hip and a signal-whistle on cord. Patched clothes, quick limbs, and a stolen cap complete the disguise of an ordinary street child. Bright restless eyes scan every lane, always measuring distances to roofs, doors, and hiding places.
payload.portrait_brief: A thin grimy face grins beneath tangled hair, with a chipped tooth and darting bright eyes. Small ears and a scabbed lip suggest street living, sudden flights, and half-healed beatings.

variants.name: Street Boy
variants.appearance_delta: A wiry young lad with a sling, whistle, and pockets full of stolen market fruit.

variants.name: Roof Runner
variants.appearance_delta: A lean older boy with rope-soled shoes, chalked hands, and scars from gutter climbs.

variants.name: Market Girl
variants.appearance_delta: A quick young girl with a basket disguise, sharp whistle, and ribbons hiding signals.

variants.name: Alley Sister
variants.appearance_delta: An older girl with a shawl, quiet shoes, and authority over younger corner watchers.

state_poses.description: He crouches perched on a rooftop edge with whistle ready, scanning lanes for approaching patrols.
He hurls stones with a sling in quick looping throws before sprinting toward the next roof.
He cowers with arms wrapped around his head as blows scatter his sling and whistle.
He sits bound against a wall with his whistle cord cut and sling confiscated.

payload.body: Enforcers collect debts and hold street corners for gang bosses who claim narrow lanes the successor guards cannot patrol. They are broad laborers and discharged soldiers turned to muscle after promised imperial pay finally dried up. Shopkeepers fear their heavy knock more than thieves, for they methodically and silently break fingers as living ledgers. Courts jail them whenever caught, but wealthy bosses pay imposed heavy fines quickly and reclaim their muscle. In open combat they are the true fighters of the gang, swinging clubs and chains with brawler skill. They stand firmly their ground where lesser cutpurses flee, guarding frightened runners positioned carefully behind them. They spare debtors who pay promptly and maim those who stall, making bleeding public examples of hesitation. Travelers learn to walk wide around claimed lanes at night, reading chalk warnings and avoiding lit lanterns. Each broken finger teaches a street its ledger, and fresh muscle always waits hungrily behind the boss.
payload.base_appearance: A heavy brawler fills doorways in a sleeveless vest, with scarred brows, chained fists, and a knotted club. Tattoos, brass rings, and debt tallies mark thick arms built for breaking shutters and fingers. A rolling gait and squared shoulders promise violence long before the first threat is spoken.
payload.portrait_brief: A broad battered face scowls beneath a scarred brow, with a flattened nose and missing tooth. Small hard eyes and a split lip convey temper, obedience to bosses, and casual cruelty.

variants.name: Young Muscle
variants.appearance_delta: A thick young man with fresh tattoos, new club, and eagerness to prove his worth.

variants.name: Pockmarked Veteran
variants.appearance_delta: An older scarred brawler with chain-wrapped fists, deaf ear, and patient menace.

variants.name: Hard Brawler
variants.appearance_delta: A broad young woman with bound fists, cropped hair, and a debt ledger tattoo.

variants.name: Older Matron
variants.appearance_delta: A heavy older woman with a cudgel, grey braid, and authority over corner crews.

state_poses.description: He stands squared with club grounded, rolling his shoulders while blocking the lane ahead.
He sweeps the club in a heavy arc meant to shatter knees and barricades together.
He shakes his battered head and staggers, blood threading from his scarred brow.
He lies flat on his back with club fallen and chain unraveled across the cobbles.

payload.body: Loan sharks lend seed-grain and shop-stakes at crushing merciless rates in towns where honest lenders fear to tread. Often failed desperate merchants themselves, they keep neat ruinous books recording debts that harvests can never clear. Debtors dread harvest season more than winter, for the shark's hard men arrive promptly with the threshing. Law permits the paper but never the beatings, a careful legal line these patient sharks cross nightly. They fight poorly in person, hiding behind hired enforcers and striking desperately only with a dagger when trapped. Their true power is the ledger, never the blade, and burning it frees entire frightened indebted streets. Folk whisper their names but sign anyway whenever hungry children cry quietly for bread at night. A dead shark's heavy debts pass to crueler kin, so killing one rarely frees anyone for long. Each signed paper plants next year's bitter harvest of fear, and clerks copy obligations by patient candlelight.
payload.base_appearance: A sleek moneylender glides in tailored coats, with ink-stained cuffs, a dagger cane, and a heavy purse. Rings, seals, and folded contracts crowd the pockets, beneath oiled hair and a practiced reassuring smile. Soft hands and polished boots declare someone who profits while hired muscle performs the beatings.
payload.portrait_brief: A smooth calculating face smiles beneath oiled hair, with thin lips and eyes like counting beads. A trimmed beard and heavy signet convey respectable menace, patience, and perfect memory for debts.

variants.name: Slick Clerk
variants.appearance_delta: A neat young man with ink fingers, false sympathy, and contracts folded inside his coat.

variants.name: Grey Master
variants.appearance_delta: An older lender with silver temples, quiet voice, and books recording half the street.

variants.name: Sharp Widow
variants.appearance_delta: A composed woman in dark jewelry whose sweet smile accompanies ruinous repayment terms.

variants.name: Young Reckoner
variants.appearance_delta: A quick young woman with tally sticks, sharp arithmetic, and no mercy for debtors.

state_poses.description: He raises one palm in commanding order while enforcers shift forward to emphasize the debt.
He jabs with his dagger cane in short frightened thrusts when debtors resist collection.
He clutches his fine coat and stumbles backward, contracts scattering across the counting table.
He kneels among torn ledgers with his purse emptied and cane snapped in two.

payload.body: Pit bosses run illegal fighting cellars in ore and garrison towns where bored laborers bet monthly wages on blood. They were brawlers themselves before age taught them to profit from younger desperate fists and broken noses. Crowds love and fear them together, for they fix bouts and severely punish loose talkers without mercy. Authorities raid the pits regularly, but well-bribed guards always warn the crowded cellars ahead of time. In combat these bosses remain genuinely dangerous, fighting with scarred knuckle-irons and seasoned grappler craft. They duel travelers who mock the house, seeking prolonged public shame rather than corpses on the stained sand. Their hired champions stand beside them whenever real armed trouble threatens the crowded betting tables and profits. Villagers blame the pits for every missing son, and mothers curse the hidden cellar doors at night. Each fixed bout feeds rumors for a season, while fresh fighters arrive hungry and desperate from the mines.
payload.base_appearance: A barrel-chested veteran looms over betting tables, with knuckle-irons on both fists and a slate at the hip. Scarred ears, flattened nose, and chalked palms mark decades spent inside sawdust fighting cellars. A heavy purse, iron keys, and oilskin coat declare ownership of blood, wagers, and silence.
payload.portrait_brief: A battered fleshy face grins beneath a scarred brow, with cauliflower ears and split lips. Small calculating eyes and a broken nose convey greed, menace, and long experience with odds.

variants.name: Scarred Youth
variants.appearance_delta: A young fighter with fresh scars, new irons, and hunger for purses and reputation.

variants.name: Fat Elder
variants.appearance_delta: An older heavy boss with jeweled slate, wheezing laugh, and champions for real fighting.

variants.name: Hard Fighter

variants.name: Older Keeper

He drives a hooking uppercut upward with knuckle-irons aimed at jaw and ribs.
He staggers sideways spitting blood, shaking his head as the crowd roars for more.
He lies sprawled across the overturned betting table with slate shattered and purse stolen.

payload.body: Contraband bosses command whole smuggling crews along deltas and marsh roads, standing far above common smugglers in coin and cruelty. They own swift boats and sturdy carts bought with untaxed profit, paying river folk generously to look away. Unlike lone smugglers they bribe patrols and hire seasoned blades, growing bold enough to tax rival crews. Folk call them river kings in nervous jest, then quietly pay the jest-toll at every landing. Law wants them more than any common thief, but unfortunate witnesses have a habit of vanishing. In battle they fight with sword and heavy purse, flanked by loyal crew and retreating by boat when pressed. They murder informers as settled policy, leaving cold bodies at lonely fords as warnings to others. Their cipher-books map every hidden landing, debt, and bribed patrol along the winding delta channels. Each drowned informer buys another season of silence, while new crews swear loyalty for silver.
payload.base_appearance: A fur-trimmed captain commands the landing in a boat-cloak, with a short sword, signet of debt, and oiled leathers. Charts, cipher-books, and tribute purses hang at the belt, beneath silver rings and a commander's confident stance. Weathered authority and tailored wealth combine into someone who taxes both smugglers and patrols alike.
payload.portrait_brief: A hardened commanding face studies the river beneath a fur collar, with grey eyes and a thin scar. A trimmed beard and heavy signet convey wealth, ruthlessness, and absolute memory for betrayals.

variants.name: Young Captain
variants.appearance_delta: An ambitious young commander with a new sword, fast boat, and hunger for larger crews.

variants.name: Grey Boss
variants.appearance_delta: An older leader with silver hair, cipher-books, and patrols already bought for seasons.

variants.name: River Queen
variants.appearance_delta: A commanding woman in boat-cloak and furs whose word rules every hidden landing.

variants.name: Older Quartermaster
variants.appearance_delta: A grey veteran with tally boards, tribute chests, and authority over shares and punishments.

state_poses.description: She stands with arms folded in command aboard the deck, crew arrayed obediently behind her.
She cuts with her short sword in practiced strokes while crew hooks drag foes closer.
She reels backward toward the rail, charts scattering as the deck tilts beneath her.
She lies slumped across scattered charts with signet torn away and crew fled.

payload.body: Roadside thugs haunt thin stretches of lonely trade road between farm belts and forest edges where patrols pass seldom. They are failed laborers and hungry deserters who learned that a drawn knife earns faster than an honest hoe. Travelers fear their sharp whistle from dark treelines far more than wolves or harsh winter weather. Nearby villages pay them off with grain rather than blood, buying uneasy seasonal passage for their carts. Law hangs them whenever caught, but the lonely roads stretch long and patrols remain painfully thin. In combat they are straightforward and brutal, rushing forward with club and knife without feint or plan. They break quickly at the first organized resistance, yet they maul lone frightened walkers without mercy. They share loot in rough equal parts and abandon wounded companions callously to the crows. Each hanged thug warns the road briefly, while hunger drives fresh hungry deserters into the treeline.
payload.base_appearance: A ragged footpad blocks the roadside in patched leathers, with a heavy club, road dust, and hungry eyes. Rope belts, stolen boots, and a short knife complete the crude kit of a desperate ambusher. A slouched stance and scarred hands suggest failed farms, abandoned ranks, and empty purses.
payload.portrait_brief: A coarse unshaven face glares beneath matted hair, with a crooked nose and yellowed teeth. Narrow suspicious eyes and a scarred chin convey hunger, violence, and readiness to whistle.

variants.name: Young Deserter
variants.appearance_delta: A gaunt young runaway with a stolen spear, cracked boots, and fear of patrols.

variants.name: Bearded Ambusher
variants.appearance_delta: An older bearded lurker with a weighted club, net, and patience for slow caravans.

variants.name: Hard Marcher
variants.appearance_delta: A lean young woman with a cudgel, bedroll, and road-wise suspicious eyes.

variants.name: Older Camp Keeper
variants.appearance_delta: A grey older woman with cooking pots, bandages, and authority over the campfire.

state_poses.description: He slouches beside the roadside ditch with club grounded, whistling signals to hidden companions.
He rushes forward with a chopping blow aimed at heads, wheels, and baggage ropes.
He reels backward clutching his arm as organized guards close ranks around him.
He lies face-down in the roadside ditch with club fallen and loot scattered.

payload.body: Toll brutes seize narrow bridges and shallow fords, demanding heavy coin from every laden cart that must cross daily. Bigger and heavier than common cutpurses, they rely on the deep swift river doing half of the threatening. Boatmen and carters hate them worst of all, for no safe detour exists around deep black churning water. Petty lords sometimes license their extortion openly, accepting quiet regular cuts from every collected toll. In battle they fight with staff and sheer weight, shoving struggling victims toward the cold black water. They hold their ground at narrow crossings where superior numbers count for much less than courage. They flee only when crossings are firmly held against them by organized guards with bows. Their carved toll-marks scar wooden posts for seasons, warning wary travelers long after they finally leave. Each broken toll-post invites another brute, while rivers keep flowing and carts must still cross daily.
payload.base_appearance: A hulking guard blocks the crossing with a quarterstaff, toll-box at the hip, and soaked boots. Broad shoulders, scarred knuckles, and a heavy barricade declare ownership of bridge, ford, and passage. Standing water, river mud, and collected coins cling to every fold of his stained clothing.
payload.portrait_brief: A heavy jowled face sweats beneath a leather cap, with small greedy eyes and a flat nose. A thick neck and stubbled chin convey stubborn weight, slow anger, and absolute territorial certainty.

variants.name: Young Heavy
variants.appearance_delta: A massive young man with a new staff, loud voice, and eagerness to shove.

variants.name: Bearded Keeper
variants.appearance_delta: An older bearded collector with toll-box, tally stick, and swollen knuckles.

variants.name: Broad Warden
variants.appearance_delta: A broad young woman with a staff, rope belt, and command of the ford.

variants.name: Older Collector
variants.appearance_delta: A grey older woman with coin scales, ledger, and patience for arguing drovers.

state_poses.description: He stands with arms crossed squarely across the bridge, staff planted like a gate.
He shoves forward with his quarterstaff, driving victims toward the churning water below.
He spins with a staggered step, arms flailing as his toll-box spills coins.
He lies toppled in the riverside mud with staff broken and toll-box overturned.

payload.body: Alley muggers work the poorest quarters of crowded trade towns where narrow lanes twist past shuttered abandoned shops. Quicker than heavy toll brutes and crueler than petty cutpurses, they strike suddenly from dark reeking nearby doorways. Frightened night walkers fear their paired rush most, with one attacker holding victims while another strips carried valuables. They know every watch-bell intimately and vanish silently before pursuing heavy boots ever reach the distant corner. In combat they swarm isolated victims with sharp drawn knives together, scattering quickly from organized armored guards. They deliberately target drunks and friendless strangers, wisely sparing locals who might later identify them in daylight. Their cuts are shallow but cruelly numerous, leaving victims frightened, bleeding, and permanently wiser about dark lanes. Shuttered shops and narrow twisting lanes give these patient attackers reliable cover night after night. Each mugging teaches wary travelers to avoid poor quarters, while hunger keeps the dark reeking doorways occupied.
payload.base_appearance: A lean lurker presses against shadowed walls in dark wraps, with twin knives, quick eyes, and silent shoes. Cord belts, stolen cloaks, and muffled buckles complete the quiet uniform of a doorway hunter. Tense readiness and sidelong glances mark someone who measures purses, escorts, and escape routes constantly.
payload.portrait_brief: A sharp hungry face hides within dark wraps, with restless eyes and a thin scarred mouth. Close-cropped hair and a corded neck convey speed, desperation, and familiarity with gutters.

variants.name: Wiry Youth
variants.appearance_delta: A thin young man with twin knives, quick feet, and a doorway already chosen.

variants.name: Scarred Holder
variants.appearance_delta: An older scarred grappler with strong arms, rope, and grip for holding victims.

variants.name: Swift Girl
variants.appearance_delta: A fast young woman with short blades, bound hair, and knowledge of every shortcut.

variants.name: Older Stripper
variants.appearance_delta: An older woman with nimble fingers, sack, and practiced speed at stripping valuables.

state_poses.description: She waits pressed flat against the alley wall, breath held as footsteps approach the corner.
She slashes in a paired rush with twin knives aimed at belts, sleeves, and hands.
She sprawls backward across wet cobbles, knives skittering away as the watch bell rings.
She sits pinned against shuttered doors with wrists bound and knives confiscated by guards.

payload.body: Caravan raiders strike slow heavy wagons on open valley and foothill roads where rising dust hides their numbers and swallows warning cries. Better armed than common roadside thugs, they always ride scavenged ponies and carry short bows with stolen arrows and spare strings. Drovers dread their tall dust-cloud at rocky narrow passes, and horns with strong escorts decide who keeps cargo and who walks home. They ransom whole laden trains rather than murder, for dead merchants draw armies that close roads for entire seasons. In battle they harass guards with arrows first, then rush stragglers fiercely while avoiding pitched fights and solid shield walls. They camp in broken hill country beyond easy pursuit, and move with the seasons while feeding their ponies on stolen fodder. Their leaders keep careful count of ransoms like merchants, recording every payment and debt in notched tally sticks. Strong escorts and loud horn-signals turn them aside toward weaker, less guarded prey traveling dark roads at dusk. Each paid ransom funds another season of saddles and arrows, while stout defiance teaches caravans to hire guards and sound horns.
payload.base_appearance: A mounted raider looms through dust in a stolen harness, with bow, saber, and a trailing dust-cloak. Scavenged saddles, mismatched armor, and rope hobbles mark a fighter supplied entirely by captured trains. A hard seat and scanning gaze suggest someone who reads dust, tracks, and escort strength expertly.
payload.portrait_brief: A dust-caked face squints beneath a wrapped scarf, with sunburned cheeks and a chipped tooth. Narrow ranging eyes and a dry mouth convey thirst, patience, and constant calculation of odds.

variants.name: Older Wrangler

state_poses.description: He circles at a mounted trot with bow half-drawn, measuring the escort before committing.
He dives low for a slashing saber-cut against drivers, outriders, and baggage ropes.
He staggers unhorsed in the dust, clutching his mount's reins as arrows fall around him.
He kneels grounded with raised hands, his pony captured and saber surrendered to guards.

payload.body: Door bouncers guard gambling cellars and fences' shops as hired fists at dangerous illicit doors where tempers run hot. Chosen purely for enormous size, they end trouble with throws and bone-cracking holds rather than blades and spilled blood. Patrons respect their massive scarred arms more than any law operating quietly inside the crowded establishment. They answer directly to pit bosses and gang enforcers, holding their posts calmly through noise, smoke, and nightly brawls. In combat they grapple and hurl grown foes expertly, remaining dangerous even while completely unarmed and outnumbered. Weapons make them slower and clumsier, though they can still block narrow entrances against armed and desperate intruders. They hold tight cramped doorways where poor footing limits every intruder's movement and cancels numerical advantage. They rarely chase trouble farther than the building's outer step, returning quickly to their post before rivals notice. Each thrown troublemaker advertises the door's safety for seasons, while frightened regulars drink easier behind broad shoulders.
payload.base_appearance: A massive doorman fills the frame with bare arms, grappling belt, and bruised professional knuckles. Strapped wrists, padded vest, and scarred ears mark a career spent throwing bodies down steps. Planted feet and folded arms promise that nothing enters or leaves without his permission.
payload.portrait_brief: A heavy impassive face stares past visitors, with a flattened nose and small watchful eyes. A shaved head and thick neck convey immovable patience, selective hearing, and sudden violence.

variants.name: Young Ox
variants.appearance_delta: A huge young man with new belt, raw strength, and eagerness to throw his first drunk.

variants.name: Older Scarred
variants.appearance_delta: A grey veteran with cauliflower ears, taped wrists, and economy of movement.

variants.name: Tall Wrestler
variants.appearance_delta: A tall young woman with long reach, braided hair, and tournament grappling experience.

variants.name: Matron Guard
variants.appearance_delta: A broad older woman with folded arms, keys, and command over the door queue.

state_poses.description: He blocks the doorframe with crossed arms, shoulders touching both posts at once.
He seizes his foe and executes a grapple-toss that clears the steps entirely.
His head shakes slowly as he absorbs blows, staggering but never leaving the doorway.
He sits slumped against the door with arms folded, still physically blocking the entrance.

payload.body: Bread rioters rise in hungry towns when grain prices outrun daily wages after two failed harvests and empty granaries. They are bakers' wives, laborers, and angry desperate youths, not soldiers, armed only with stones and heavy staves. Folk pity and fear them together, for their cause is just and righteous while their spreading fire burns quickly. Authorities answer with water and batons first, reserving edged steel only if granaries and guarded stores burn. In combat they swarm and shove in dense angry crowds, dangerous together yet helpless when isolated and alone. They break quickly once recognized leaders fall to batons, melting back into workshops and crowded dark tenements. Their barricades of overturned carts vanish by morning, leaving only cold ash and angry painted slogans. Travelers avoid market squares on riot days, reading distant smoke and listening carefully for warning bells. Each riot lowers bread prices for a season, while empty granaries promise another hungry spring and fiercer crowds.
payload.base_appearance: A flour-dusted townsfolk advances in apron and shawl, with a stave, stones, and work-worn hands. Patched clothes, hungry faces, and carpentry tools mark ordinary people driven past endurance. Soiled hems and rolled sleeves suggest bakers, porters, and mothers rather than trained fighters.
payload.portrait_brief: A flushed angry face shouts beneath a flour-caked headscarf, with red eyes and bared teeth. A gaunt cheek and bitten lip convey hunger, grief, and sudden communal courage.

variants.name: Young Laborer
variants.appearance_delta: A lean young workman with a stave, dusty coat, and hunger sharpened by missed meals.

variants.name: Grey Baker
variants.appearance_delta: An older flour-white baker with rolling pin, burned forearms, and ruined livelihood.

variants.name: Market Wife
variants.appearance_delta: A stout young mother with a basket, stones, and fury for her children's hunger.

variants.name: Young Daughter
variants.appearance_delta: A thin girl with a sling, patched shawl, and a voice in the chanting crowd.

state_poses.description: She advances shouting with stave raised, shoulder to shoulder inside the surging crowd.
She hurls a stone overhead toward shutters, granaries, and the helmets beyond.
She stumbles scattering backward as batons break the front rank of the march.
She sits with hands raised among overturned carts, apron torn and stave surrendered.

payload.body: Deserter captains lead bands of runaway soldiers who refuse empty pay and endless freezing winter marches. They keep strict drill and faded patched banners, living off forced levies collected across lonely high hill country. Villagers feed them from fear and old habit, remembering uncomfortably that they were once sworn protectors. Commanders hunt them as examples to others, offering false pardons as bait and hemp ropes as the alternative. In battle they are the most disciplined rebels anywhere, fighting in ordered ranks with spear and shield. They withdraw in good order rather than rout, carrying wounded comrades and grounded banners together off the field. They parley for pardons between raids, writing careful letters through priests and reluctant frightened merchants. Their continued desertion spreads quietly if regular pay stays thin through another campaign season and winter. Each spared village pays again next season, while recruiters find fewer willing spears every single year.
payload.base_appearance: A weathered officer holds the line in a dented cuirass, with spear, faded sash, and patched boots. Regulation kit, mended straps, and a banner pole mark discipline surviving beyond lawful service. A straight back and level gaze command obedience from men the empire has already abandoned.
payload.portrait_brief: A stern sun-lined face studies the field beneath a dented helm, with grey eyes and clipped beard. A scarred jaw and tight mouth convey command, grievance, and exhausted professional pride.

variants.name: Young Lieutenant
variants.appearance_delta: A sharp young officer with a new sash, bright spear, and ideals not yet broken.

variants.name: Grey Captain

variants.name: Hard Sergeant

variants.name: Older Quartermaster
variants.appearance_delta: A grey veteran with levy books, grain tallies, and control over shares and rations.

state_poses.description: He stands in an ordered line with spear leveled, shield overlapping the soldier beside him.
He thrusts with his spear in disciplined unison, stepping forward behind the shield wall.
He braces behind his shield and staggers, holding the line as ranks close around him.
He kneels with grounded spear, banner planted upright while awaiting terms or judgment.

payload.body: Hedge preachers gather ragged crowds in open fields and barns, blaming tolls and hunger on corrupt stewards. They carry no weapon but their practiced silver tongue, yet their fierce words arm listening crowds with stones. Listeners bring food and hide them from patrols, sheltering voices that speak their own buried grievances aloud. Authorities arrest them for sedition, unintentionally making martyrs whose names outlive every sentence and sheriff. In combat they fight weakly with a plain staff, always shielded by devoted believers forming living walls. Their true strength is leadership, holding frightened mobs together under blows that would scatter paid mercenaries. Capture them and surrounding crowds thin quickly, for borrowed courage needs its lender standing nearby. Their sermons promise the old empire's justice without naming heirs, thrones, or successor regimes aloud. Any hedge-sermon blessing capacity remains a flagged folk proposal under magic doctrine, never final canon law, while magistrates watch and wait. Burned sermons outlive their preachers, and frightened villages remember martyrs for generations afterward.
payload.base_appearance: A travel-worn speaker climbs a fieldstone in patched robes, with a staff and satchel of handwritten tracts. Hoarse voice, raised arms, and ink-stained fingers mark endless sermons delivered across farming villages. Mud-caked hems and a weathered face promise someone who sleeps in barns, not inns.
payload.portrait_brief: A gaunt fervent face burns beneath a hood, with bright eyes and a mouth shaped by sermons. Lined cheeks and a grey beard convey hardship, conviction, and practiced persuasive sorrow.

variants.name: Young Speaker
variants.appearance_delta: A fiery young man with a new staff, loud voice, and crowds of fellow youths.

variants.name: Bearded Elder
variants.appearance_delta: An older preacher with a grey beard, worn tracts, and authority over whole villages.

variants.name: Stern Widow

variants.name: Young Prophetess

state_poses.description: He addresses the crowd with both arms raised high, tracts clutched against his chest.
He swings his walking staff in a wide arc to shield himself from closing guards.
He staggers bowed beneath blows, still shielding fallen listeners with his own body.
He kneels bound before the magistrate, head bowed but voice still preaching to onlookers.

payload.body: Toll breakers smash toll-gates and burn hated tax posts along roads burdened with triple duties and bribes. They are carters and drovers who decided that armed tribute costs more than open rebellion and prison. Traders secretly cheer their work while publicly condemning every splintered beam and every freed cart. Guards rebuild each burned post patiently, knowing hammers will visit again before the next harvest. In combat they wield sledge and axe against wood and men alike, made strong by years of labor. They strike at grey dawn and melt into friendly farms, leaving broken beams as their proud signature. They spare ordinary travelers and share seized coin with villages that sheltered them overnight from patrols. Their marks of broken beams warn the next post, and nervous garrisons read them with growing dread. Each burned post lowers collections for a season, while new breakers learn the hammer's trade from veterans. Broken gates cost the toll lords dearly, and village carpenters quietly thank the hammer.
payload.base_appearance: A burly carter shoulders a sledgehammer, with a necklace of collected toll-tokens and scorched sleeves. Leather apron, iron-shod boots, and rope belts mark a laborer turned deliberate rebel. Broad shoulders and burned hands promise someone who breaks oak gates, not just arguments.
payload.portrait_brief: A broad defiant face grins beneath a sweat-soaked headband, with a broken tooth and bright eyes. A heavy jaw and scarred brow convey labor, anger, and stubborn popular pride.

variants.name: Young Driver

variants.name: Older Smith

state_poses.description: He faces the toll-gate with sledge grounded, measuring the beam before the first swing.

He lies sprawled across the broken gate with sledge fallen and tokens scattered.

payload.body: Student agitators are clerk-school youths printing fiery broadsides against stewards and leading street marches, and plastering walls with ink by night. They are quick with words and pamphlets but slow with blades and bloody street fighting. Townsfolk admire their fire until angry crowds begin throwing stones at shuttered windows and guards. Masters expel them publicly in disgrace, while jails steadily fill with captured students every single term. In combat they are weak rebels waving knives and torches noisily rather than effectively against armor. They rally others skillfully with slogans rather than personally winning difficult fights against trained guards. Their ink-stained hands betray their work after every disrupted march through crowded market squares. Dispersing the hidden printing press causes the surrounding march to fade and scatter within days. Each confiscated press teaches subtler printing, while younger pupils inherit the hidden type and cause, while masters hire more guards. Expelled students harden into full rebels within a single season, and crowded jails graduate angrier agitators with wider followings every year.
payload.base_appearance: An ink-fingered youth waves a broadsheet in a school cloak, with a satchel of sheets and short knife. Stained cuffs, smudged cheeks, and a printer's apron mark long nights over hidden presses. Bright restless energy and loud slogans promise more courage in print than in melee.
payload.portrait_brief: A young flushed face shouts beneath tousled hair, with ink-spotted cheeks and burning eyes. A stubborn chin and quick mouth convey learning, outrage, and youthful invulnerable certainty.

payload.body: Free spears sell their shields seasonally to employers feeding caravans and busy quarry work gangs, and guarding harvest fairs in autumn. They are landless farm children who learned drill from retired soldiers in dusty village squares. Employers value their steady unbroken line more than any exceptional personal courage or glory. Villagers also hire them as reliable guards during harvests and crowded autumn livestock markets. In combat they are solid spear-and-shield infantry, neither fierce nor brittle under heavy pressure. They hold their ground faithfully while paid in coin, and leave promptly when wages run out. They rarely hate their foes or pursue personal vendettas beyond the contract's written terms. Their contracts are sealed with handclasps instead of binding oaths, and both sides remember the bargain. Each completed contract buys another season's reputation, while broken ones follow them for years between towns, closing wealthy doors and rich contracts. Loyal spears recommend their captains to new employers, and a file that never broke finds work in every season.
payload.base_appearance: A plain pikeman stands ready with spear and patched shield, marching boots laced for long roads. Simple harness, bedroll, and ration pouch mark a professional without household or livery. A level stance and quiet eyes promise contracted steadiness rather than heroic ambition.
payload.portrait_brief: An open weathered face watches calmly beneath a plain helm, with steady eyes and sunburned nose. A firm mouth and cropped hair convey reliability, modesty, and professional patience.

variants.name: Young Recruit

payload.body: Coin bows are hired archers from forest-edge hamlets who track game and armed people with equal patience. They guard herds and ambush rival convoys faithfully in exchange for seasonal pay and winter grain. Their early ranging arrows feed employers long before any larger battle properly begins in earnest. Folk hire them against wolves as readily as against thieves on lonely forest roads. In combat they shoot from deep cover first, then withdraw quietly with knives when pressed hard, melting between trees like smoke. They avoid melee deliberately because their survival and wages depend upon maintaining safe range. They quit lost causes early rather than waste valuable arrows on hopeless and bloody stands. Their bowstrings are their livelihood, carefully oiled and waxed every single night without fail. Each spent arrow is counted against wages, so they loose only clean shots they fully trust, counting every shaft against their pay. Master bowmen train village youths for a share of wages, and forest hamlets never lack for arrows.
payload.base_appearance: A lean archer melts into cover in green wraps, with a short bow, full quiver, and silent boots. Bracers, spare strings, and a skinning knife complete the light kit of a woodland professional. A still posture and slow breathing promise patience learned from hunting wary game.
payload.portrait_brief: A narrow forest face watches beneath a hood, with keen eyes and a scarred cheek. A quiet mouth and weathered skin convey patience, distance, and careful arithmetic of shots.

payload.body: Camp blades are hangers-on turned fighters who cook, mend, and rob battlefields between hires and campaigns, following drums for bread and loot. They know intimately the leavings left behind by every passing army on the long march. Soldiers mock them openly in camp but still employ them for necessary dirty work. In combat they fight scrappily with cleavers and cudgels in disorderly hungry packs. They loot first and fight only when protecting loot strictly requires it of them, though they prefer running to fighting. Their carts follow every column, searching patiently for food, salvage, and abandoned equipment. Peace leaves them hungry and frequently drives them into thievery along quiet country roads. Their layered rags conceal tools useful for cooking, mending, and quiet theft alike. Each campaign teaches new scavenging routes, while peace sends them begging at garrison gates for scraps, until the next war calls. Old camp blades settle as sutlers and storytellers, and young soldiers pay coin to hear of past campaigns.
payload.base_appearance: A grease-stained follower guards a laden pack-cart, with a cleaver, layered rags, and sharp eyes. Pots, needles, and pry-hooks hang among the bundles of a walking salvage market. A shuffling gait and darting glance promise someone who survives on leavings and opportunity.
payload.portrait_brief: A soot-smudged hungry face peers from layered hoods, with a broken tooth and quick eyes. A pinched mouth and scarred hands convey cooking, mending, and opportunistic theft.

variants.name: Young Cook
variants.appearance_delta: A thin young lad with a ladle, kitchen knife, and hunger for scraps.

variants.name: Scarred Scavenger

payload.body: Siege hands are laborers skilled with rams, ladders, and mattocks during brutal walled assaults and sieges, where pay runs high and life runs short. Quarry and mine work has given them notably broad backs and exceptionally steady nerves under fire. Garrison towns dread their arrival even more than mounted knights battering at the gates. In combat they strike slowly but crush foes with heavy mauls and stout timber shields. They are deadly at gates and breaches but clumsy and exposed across open level ground, crushing gates and bones alike. They dig and hammer under fire whenever commanders require breaches opened before nightfall. Their pay runs higher whenever a dangerous breach assignment awaits brave volunteers. Without walls to break, they hire themselves out as guards and debt enforcers. Each breached gate teaches defenders to fear picks, while sappers count extra wages and scars, and drink to fallen mates. Retired siege hands become quarry masters and sappers' teachers, and fortress commanders pay well for their counsel.
payload.base_appearance: A massive laborer braces beneath a timber shield, with a maul, rope harness, and quarry dust. Helm, padding, and iron-shod boots mark someone accustomed to falling masonry and arrows. Towering shoulders and scarred forearms promise crushing strength at gates and breaches.
payload.portrait_brief: A broad dust-caked face squints beneath a leather helm, with a flattened nose and cracked lips. Heavy brows and a stone-chip scar convey labor, endurance, and indifference to danger.

variants.name: Young Quarryman
variants.appearance_delta: A huge young laborer with a new maul, loud strength, and hunger for breach pay.

variants.name: Bald Veteran

He sits slumped on broken rubble with maul fallen and shield splintered.

payload.body: War dog handlers lead mastiff packs for patrols and debt-taking where scattered people are few and far, where teeth speak louder than laws. They raise pups using blood rewards and sharp whistle commands from their earliest weaning days. Villagers fear the slathering war dogs more deeply than their quiet scarred masters. Local law holds the masters liable for every serious bite and every torn flock. In combat they send dogs first through gates, then strike from behind them with long spears. Handler and pack fight as a coordinated pair against surprised and separated opponents on patrols. If the dogs fall to blades, their handlers quickly lose heart and abandon the field. Their leashes and whistles clearly mark them among ordinary travelers on lonely country roads. Each trained litter extends the kennel's reputation, while dead dogs bankrupt their keepers within seasons, and empty kennels howl at night. Famous kennels sell pups to lords and patrols, and a proven bloodline commands princely prices across three valleys.
payload.base_appearance: A hide-aproned handler advances behind leashed mastiffs, with a spear, whistle-cord, and scarred forearms. Leashes, muzzles, and meat pouches mark a professional built around teeth and obedience. A low stance and constant whistling promise coordinated violence between human and pack.
payload.portrait_brief: A lean weathered face watches past the pack, with a split lip and dog-scratched cheek. Calm commanding eyes and a scarred ear convey authority over animals and unease among people.

variants.name: Young Kennel Lad

variants.name: Scarred Master

variants.name: Older Breeder

payload.body: Hired blades are practiced fighters whose discipline sets them clearly above ordinary outlaws and desperate brigands. They sell their swords to caravans, households, and threatened traveling parties through every dangerous season. Daily drills keep their blades oiled and their footwork reliably sharp for sudden emergencies on the road. Employers trust their steady hands when danger gathers around guarded gates late at night. Villagers sometimes pool scarce coin to hire them against predatory gangs and cruel seasonal raiders, demanding honest steel for honest coin. In combat they remain balanced and patient, parrying carefully before answering with measured ripostes. They withdraw promptly when contracts end, rather than fleeing in sudden panic like cheaper blades. Their reputation determines their wage, and broken contracts ruin all future hires across neighboring towns. Each honored contract brings better employers and richer purses, while broken ones follow them between towns for years, shadowing every hiring negotiation. Veteran blades retire as drill masters and tavern guards, and their names open doors in every garrison town.
payload.base_appearance: A clean sellsword waits in balanced guard, with an arming sword, buckler, and maintained harness. Oiled leather, sharpened steel, and mended straps mark a professional who drills daily. A relaxed stance and level gaze promise competence without wasted swagger or threats.
payload.portrait_brief: A composed watchful face studies the employer beneath a plain helm, with steady grey eyes. A trimmed jaw and small scar convey experience, honesty about limits, and professional calm.

variants.name: Young Sword

variants.name: Weathered Veteran

payload.body: Dueling tutors teach blade manners to merchants' sons and ambitious young guard officers seeking promotion, and paying in gold for polish. They take temporary hires between lessons to maintain their own standing and supplement their income. Their polished elegant style comes from school-yards rather than harsh muddy battlefields and ditches. Proud students boast loudly about the masters who taught their admired flourishes and disarms. In combat tutors are precise and showy, preferring humiliating disarms over deaths and ugly wounds. They may challenge travelers who publicly insult their favored pupils in crowded taverns at night, defending pupils' honor loudly. Their costly private lessons often earn more than ordinary hired work across a whole season. A humiliating lost duel can empty an instructor's entire school within a matter of weeks. Each victorious pupil advertises the school for years, while defeated ones quietly seek other masters elsewhere. Famous tutors write manuals and judge tournaments, and their certificates raise a pupil's price enormously.
payload.base_appearance: A slim instructor salutes in a padded jack, with a foil, chalked hands, and precise footwork. Practice padding, spare blades, and a master's sash mark the school-yard rather than the battlefield. An upright posture and deliberate gestures promise lessons in timing, distance, and pride.
payload.portrait_brief: A refined narrow face regards the pupil over a foil, with arched brows and cool eyes. A thin mustache and powdered cheek convey vanity, precision, and practiced condescension.

variants.name: Young Graduate
variants.appearance_delta: A fresh young instructor with a bright foil, new sash, and memorized forms.

variants.name: Older Master

variants.name: Older Matron

payload.body: Bodyguards shadow wealthy travelers and paymasters, paid to bleed before their clients on dangerous roads, sleeping lightly across doorways. They are chosen for loyalty and vigilance rather than flashy swordplay and public reputation. Their watchful eyes study crowds more carefully than any individual blade approaching through the press. Households sleep more easily when a bodyguard stands watch beside their bolted doors. In combat they interpose bodies and shields, striking only to clear space around threatened charges, spending their own bodies freely. They retreat alongside their charges rather than chasing defeated attackers for glory or purses. Every scar marks a life they successfully kept from harm through vigilance and pain. A dead charge can end a bodyguard's entire trade across every hiring town for years. Each protected journey builds quiet reputation, while one grisly failure closes every wealthy door forever, and blackens their name for years. Trusted bodyguards inherit their charges' households and secrets, and grateful widows pension them for life.
payload.base_appearance: A broad shield-bearer shadows the client with a tower shield, short sword, and constant scanning. Reinforced bracers, plain livery, and scarred armor mark someone hired to absorb blades. A close hovering stance promises interception before any threat reaches the charge.
payload.portrait_brief: A heavy vigilant face scans the crowd over the shield rim, with tired loyal eyes. A square jaw and flattened nose convey endurance, obedience, and practiced suspicion.

variants.name: Young Shield
variants.appearance_delta: A strong young guard with a new shield, bright eyes, and untested loyalty.

variants.name: Older Oathman
variants.appearance_delta: A grey veteran with a dented shield, slow step, and lives saved remembered.

variants.name: Stern Guard
variants.appearance_delta: A severe young woman with a tower shield, braided hair, and absolute focus.

variants.name: Older Protector
variants.appearance_delta: A grey older guardian with a short sword, calm voice, and decades of watches.

state_poses.description: She stands covering her charge with shield raised, eyes sweeping the surrounding crowd.
She bashes forward with her shield to clear space, short sword following the opening.
She staggers as her shield drops low, blood threading from beneath the rim.
She kneels over her fallen charge, shield planted as a final sheltering wall.

payload.body: Road wardens are licensed blades patrolling trade stretches for toll cooperatives and merchant councils, riding circuits in all weathers. They serve as part guard and part tax collector along busy commercial routes between towns. Long patrols teach them every ambush bend along their assigned roads and hidden shortcuts. Drovers gladly pay their tolls when familiar wardens display their protective pennants at bridges. In combat they hold the road-center steadily with practical halberds and practiced teamwork, masters of the road's crown. They pursue raiders with resolve but sensibly spare travelers who pay promptly and politely. Their recognizable license marks are copied and forged surprisingly often by clever bandits. Without wardens, thugs reclaim exposed roads within only several dangerous and bloody days. Each safe convoy justifies the toll for seasons, while robbed ones cancel licenses by year's end, and ruin their cooperative. Old wardens retire as toll-keepers and route guides, and young drovers seek their counsel before journeys.
payload.base_appearance: A pennanted halberdier plants the road-center in a road-cloak, with a license badge and horn. Sturdy boots, oiled halberd, and a toll satchel mark lawful authority on lonely stretches. A planted stance and raised pennant promise protection backed by cooperative coin.
payload.portrait_brief: A weathered honest face calls the challenge beneath a broad hat, with clear eyes and sunburn. A square chin and loud voice convey authority, routine, and familiarity with drovers.

variants.name: Young Warden
variants.appearance_delta: A fresh young patroller with a new badge, bright pennant, and memorized bends.

variants.name: Grey Patrol
variants.appearance_delta: An older rider with a scarred halberd, quiet humor, and decades of roads.

variants.name: Hard Rider
variants.appearance_delta: A tough young woman with a pony, horn, and refusal to abandon convoys.

variants.name: Older Keeper
variants.appearance_delta: A grey older keeper with ledgers, spare badges, and control over the roster.

state_poses.description: He plants himself at the road-center with halberd grounded and pennant flying.
He sweeps his halberd in a wide arc to clear ambushers from ditches and banks.
He staggers dropping his horn as brigands rush past his guard in numbers.
He sits slumped at the milepost with badge dented and convoy scattered.

payload.body: Retired sergeants sell drill and muscle after long years of hard military service on frontiers, and now drill grandchildren of recruits. They shape trembling local militias and guard stored goods through dangerous hungry seasons. Their seasoned parade-ground shouts can still form disciplined lines from frightened rabble. Villagers pool scarce funds to retain one throughout each difficult hungry winter. In combat they direct allies constantly while striking short, hard, and cunningly with veteran economy, wasting no motion or breath. Their firm presence often anchors formations that would otherwise quickly rout at first blood. Their stories teach recruits more lasting lessons than their battered swords ever could. Age slows their legs considerably, but experience keeps their watchful eyes sharp and pitiless. Each drilled militia holds longer next season, while undrilled ones scatter screaming at horns, to the sergeant's disgust. Beloved sergeants are buried with honors by villages they drilled, and their sticks pass to successors.
payload.base_appearance: A grey veteran barks orders with a drill-stick, wearing a medal-stripped coat and short blade. Straight spine, scarred hands, and a parade-ground voice mark decades of commanded ranks. A planted stance and pointing stick promise that rabble can become soldiers by spring.
payload.portrait_brief: A seamed commanding face glares beneath grey brows, with a drill-field voice and flint eyes. A white mustache and battered ear convey authority, impatience, and remembered campaigns.

variants.name: Lame Trainer
variants.appearance_delta: A limping young veteran with a stick, loud voice, and endless patience for recruits.

variants.name: Bald Elder
variants.appearance_delta: An older sergeant with a polished head, short blade, and stories for every scar.

variants.name: Hard Widow-Sergeant
variants.appearance_delta: A tough widow with a drill-stick, harsh standards, and militias that hold.

variants.name: Older Drillmistress
variants.appearance_delta: A grey older instructor with a cane, sharp eyes, and authority over the square.

state_poses.description: She raises her drill-stick high, shouting the line straight as recruits shuffle into order.
She chops downward with her short blade in economical strokes between shouted commands.
Her knee buckles as she staggers, yet her voice never stops directing the line.
She sits upright giving orders, wounded leg bound while the militia holds around her.

payload.body: Knife assassins kill for coin where crowded market quarters conceal a sudden blade and escape, leaving no witness who can describe them. They accept single contracts only, taking payment before and after each quiet killing. They ask no reasons, only prices, timings, and useful descriptions of intended marks. Folk fear their quiet approach more than soldiers' noisy patrols on dark nights. The law hangs them without mercy or delay, so they work alone and masked. In open combat their paired daggers make first rushes especially deadly and shocking, ending fights before guards arrive. They seek quick clean kills before escaping swiftly through the surrounding panicked crowds. Their plain blades reveal neither masters, houses, nor easily traced origins to investigators. Each silent killing raises their price for seasons, while one captured assassin warns every mark, and doubles the price of silence. Retired assassins vanish into quiet trades and foreign towns, and no neighbor ever learns their past.
payload.base_appearance: A plain-cloaked killer drifts through crowds in soft boots, with paired daggers and a masked wrap. Unremarkable clothes, covered hair, and quiet hands mark someone forgettable by professional design. A gliding step and downcast gaze promise sudden violence from arm's length.
payload.portrait_brief: A forgettable pale face hides within a wrap, with flat eyes and an unremarkable mouth. A smooth chin and average features convey deliberate anonymity and professional emptiness.

variants.name: Young Blade
variants.appearance_delta: A lean young killer with new daggers, steady hands, and hunger for contracts.

variants.name: Pale Veteran
variants.appearance_delta: An older assassin with scarred wrists, quiet shoes, and a price for anyone.

variants.name: Quiet Girl
variants.appearance_delta: A small young woman with hidden blades, soft voice, and invisible presence in crowds.

variants.name: Older Widow
variants.appearance_delta: A grey older woman with a shawl, poison knowledge, and decades of quiet killings.

state_poses.description: He drifts in a crowd-blend stalk, hands empty and face forgettable among shoppers.
He rushes with a twin-stab burst aimed at throat and kidney before the alarm.
He staggers exposed as his mask slips, crowd turning suddenly against him.
He lies crumpled with dropped mask and daggers scattered across the stones.

payload.body: Garrotters strangle chosen marks in dark reeking lanes without spilling visible blood or raising alarms, and leave no blood for hounds. They favor debt disputes and inheritance quarrels where silent death pays best and fastest. Night walkers fear footsteps approaching from behind more than open threats and drawn steel. Garrotters carry wire loops in belt disguises resembling common work tools and aprons. In combat they grapple from behind first, then struggle desperately when forced face-to-face, where wire matters less than strength. If seized, they thrash, bite, and fight desperately for any narrow chance of escape. They commonly work as pairs, with one strong holder and one remorseless puller. Their distinctive wire marks condemn them whenever authorities catch them alive and masked. Each silent strangling feeds lane rumors for months, while increased patrols starve them for seasons, until lanes grow careless again. Hanged garrotters leave distinctive marks that teach constables, and new stranglers study their mistakes.
payload.base_appearance: A wiry strangler trails marks in a hood, with wire-loops at the belt and heavy cuffs. Workman's clothes, padded gloves, and a blank face mark a killer disguised as labor. Quiet trailing steps and coiled readiness promise death arriving from directly behind.
payload.portrait_brief: A narrow forgettable face watches from a hood, with close-set eyes and a thin mouth. A corded neck and scarred wrists convey hidden strength and professional patience.

variants.name: Thin Youth
variants.appearance_delta: A gaunt young strangler with quick hands, wire loops, and hunger for coin.

variants.name: Thick Elder
variants.appearance_delta: A heavy older killer with powerful arms, calm patience, and debts collected quietly.

variants.name: Small Woman
variants.appearance_delta: A slight young woman with hidden wire, soft steps, and underestimated strength.

variants.name: Older Cleaner
variants.appearance_delta: A grey older sweeper with a cart, broom, and wires among the tools.

state_poses.description: He trails his mark in a patient stalk, hands loose near the belt loops.
He lunges into a wire-pull grapple, cord biting as the victim thrashes.
He staggers thrown-off against the wall as the wire snaps and coils away.
He lies pinned with his cut wire displayed as evidence before the magistrate.

payload.body: Poisoners sell powders and draughts to clients who fear honest steel and open confrontation, preferring silence to steel. They work from herb stalls and dye shops without drawing notice or suspicion from neighbors. Their knowledge distinguishes gut-wrenching herbs from valuable healing ones with exact precision. Cooks and cup-bearers dread their hidden trade more than most open threats and robbers. Proven poisoners lose their shops permanently when the watch finally takes action against them. In combat they rely on prepared darts and rotating mundane dusts, never true magic of any kind, only chemistry and patience. Their advantage is careful readiness, which fades quickly after close engagement begins in earnest. They carry personal antidotes at all times and seldom share them freely with anyone. Each exposed poisoner teaches kitchens new precautions, while subtler mixers quietly inherit the trade, with subtler shops and safer clients. Exiled poisoners sell their knowledge to distant courts, and their recipes outlive their ruined shops.
payload.base_appearance: A stained herbalist hovers behind vials in a cloth mask, with careful gloves and a bandolier. Dye marks, mortar dust, and labeled jars mark legitimate trade concealing murder. Measured movements and downwind positioning promise someone who respects powders and drafts.
payload.portrait_brief: A sallow cautious face peers over a mask, with stained lips and calculating eyes. A furrowed brow and gloved chin convey knowledge, secrecy, and professional paranoia.

variants.name: Young Mixer
variants.appearance_delta: A quick young herbalist with fresh vials, keen nose, and memorized recipes.

variants.name: Pockmarked Master
variants.appearance_delta: An older mixer with scarred lungs, careful scales, and wealthy fearful clients.

variants.name: Sharp Mixer
variants.appearance_delta: A precise young woman with clean vials, steady hands, and a dye-shop front.

variants.name: Older Dyer
variants.appearance_delta: A grey older woman with vat-stained arms, herbal garden, and decades of secrets.

state_poses.description: She hovers vial-ready with one hand raised, measuring wind and distance carefully.
She tosses her dust wide, then stabs with a short blade as victims choke.
She staggers coughing in her own cloud, mask slipping as the wind turns.
She lies slumped over spilled vials with antidotes scattered just beyond reach.

payload.body: Crossbow killers shoot from upper windows and barn lofts at carefully chosen marks below, and vanish before bells ring. Many are failed soldiers or hunters preferring distance to personal daggers and grappling. Crowds scatter quickly when the first prepared bolt strikes nearby without warning or sound, scattering markets into panic. They own no uniforms, relying instead upon rented rooms and convenient high cover. In combat they fire once from hiding, then draw short swords when rushed by guards, abandoning bolts and cases. Their real craft is the prepared patient shot, never prolonged honorable melee. They abandon crossbows readily when escape demands speed and mobility through attics. Shuttered windows and zigzagging streets make their prepared attacks much harder to arrange. Each failed shot teaches towns to shutter windows, while new lofts always open for rent, and landlords ask no questions. Failed killers sell their crossbows and disappear, and rented lofts stand empty until the next contract.
payload.base_appearance: A hooded marksman waits at an upper window in a loft-cloak, with a folding crossbow and bolt-case. Rented rooms, oiled mechanisms, and measured sightlines mark a patient professional killer. A still silhouette against shutters promises one decisive shot before sudden flight.
payload.portrait_brief: A gaunt patient face watches from a hood, with one narrowed aiming eye and thin lips. A still brow and scarred cheek convey waiting, distance, and professional detachment.

variants.name: Young Hunter

variants.name: Grey Shot
variants.appearance_delta: An older marksman with a worn stock, oiled cranequin, and rented lofts across towns.

variants.name: Keen Lass
variants.appearance_delta: A sharp young woman with a light crossbow, quiet rooms, and inheritance contracts.

variants.name: Older Widow
variants.appearance_delta: A grey older woman with a curtained window, patience, and a list of debtors.

state_poses.description: He kneels in loft-aim with crossbow braced on the sill, breath held steady.

He staggers drawing his short sword as guards burst through the loft door.
He lies toppled beside his empty case with bolts scattered across the floorboards.

payload.body: Bathhouse blades strike where victims bathe or sleep unarmed, exposed, and completely trusting, wrapped in steam and helplessness. They pose as patient smiling attendants, quietly learning habits over several careful days. Hosts fear them deeply because hospitality itself becomes a concealed ambush under their hands, betraying every guest-custom held sacred. Their short blades remain hidden inside ordinary folded towels and clean linen stacks. In combat they move quickly against unarmored foes with single precise daggers, striking before victims wake. Ready guards expose their frailty and quickly limit their opportunities to strike. They flee through undressed crowds, using confusion and screams as protective cover. Locked inner doors and personal guards effectively block their patient established routines. Each exposed attendant teaches hosts to lock doors, while new smiling faces always apply, seeking wages and revenge. Exposed bathhouse killers are flayed by outraged hosts, and every innkeeper afterward locks inner doors at night, posting guards in every steam room.
payload.base_appearance: An attendant-garbed killer offers towels with damp hair, soft sandals, and a folded dagger. Clean linens, bowed head, and quiet service mark a predator disguised as hospitality. Unremarkable posture and practiced smiles promise intimate knowledge of unguarded moments.
payload.portrait_brief: A smooth servile face smiles beneath damp hair, with downcast eyes and a soft voice. A bland brow and unremarkable features convey forgettable service and hidden patience.

variants.name: Young Attendant

variants.name: Older Keeper
variants.appearance_delta: An older bath-keeper with keys, oils, and knowledge of every client's habits.

variants.name: Maid

variants.name: Older Matron
