She strikes with a close sudden stab before the victim can cry out.
She staggers as her wrist is seized, towel falling to reveal the blade.
She lies wrapped in torn sheets with the dagger kicked beyond her reach.

payload.display_name: Shinobi (male-only exception: male role tradition, 4 male variants)
payload.body: Shinobi are hired infiltrators who scale high walls and watch lonely roads for steady pay, and dangerous night work. They train upon cliffs and rooftops for years, valuing silence far above brute strength and numbers. Households dread the faint scratches heard near shuttered windows during dark nights. They carry hooks and short blades while avoiding open confrontations entirely as doctrine. In combat they evade foes constantly and stab from behind with practiced precision, vanishing before alarms sound. They are weaker during sustained stands against prepared and armored opponents in daylight. When pressed hard, they escape across roofs using practiced climbing routes and knotted ropes. Dogs and loose gravel reliably expose their otherwise silent and careful night movements. Each captured climber teaches households to keep dogs, while new trainees practice ever quieter, padding every buckle and edge. Old shinobi teach climbing and silence to new hires, and their scars map every wall in the region.
payload.base_appearance: A dark-wrapped male climber clings to eaves with hook-rope, short blade, and masked leanness. Close bindings, silent tabi, and compact tools mark a professional of roofs and walls. A low crouch and measured breathing promise entry without alarm or trace.
payload.portrait_brief: A masked lean face shows only narrowed eyes above dark wraps, with shaved head beneath. Alert watchful eyes and controlled breathing convey patience, silence, and night discipline.

variants.name: Young Creeper
variants.appearance_delta: A lithe young climber with new hooks, quick hands, and rooftop confidence.

variants.name: Scarred Scaler
variants.appearance_delta: An older infiltrator with rope scars, filed tools, and knowledge of every wall.

variants.name: Broad Diver
variants.appearance_delta: A strong swimmer with oilskin wraps, water entries, and moat experience.

variants.name: Grey Watcher
variants.appearance_delta: An older observer with far-seeing patience, signal codes, and roadside hides.

He sits netted and bound with tools confiscated and mask pulled away.

payload.display_name: Kunoichi (female-only exception: female role tradition, 4 female variants)
payload.body: Kunoichi pose as servants and errand women to overhear valuable secrets in great households, smiling behind trays and fans. They learn poison herbs and message codes alongside practiced smiles and graceful manners. Hosts most fear the familiar hands they once trusted completely with children and keys, learning lullabies and ledgers. Hairpin daggers and powder gourds remain concealed within their ordinary layered clothing. In combat they strike dazed foes after mundane ash flashes, never true magic of any kind, only powder and timing. Once exposed, they are frail against alert and ready opponents wearing armor. They vanish into crowds of women when pursuit becomes dangerous and organized. Their painted fans hide signals, while locked inner rooms block their access to targets. Each exposed servant teaches households to vet hires, while new smiling faces arrive monthly, patient as winter. Retired kunoichi marry into households they once spied upon, and carry secrets to their graves, never whispering a name.
payload.base_appearance: A servant-garbed woman glides with a fan, hairpin dagger, and powder gourd at her sash. Plain kimono layers, lowered eyes, and quiet service mark an infiltrator disguised as staff. Graceful unremarkable movements promise overheard secrets and unnoticed powders.
payload.portrait_brief: A gentle composed face smiles beneath a servant's coif, with bright observant eyes. Soft features and a practiced smile convey obedience, warmth, and hidden calculation.

variants.name: Young Maid

variants.appearance_delta: A trusted older housekeeper with keys, authority, and decades of overheard secrets.

variants.name: Grey Go-Between
variants.appearance_delta: An older messenger with market baskets, coded fans, and contacts across households.

She sits wrapped and bound with gourd confiscated and coif pulled away.

payload.display_name: Genin (young low rank, all youthful visuals)
payload.body: Genin are apprentice operatives sent on errands, watches, and their first dangerous thefts, earning bruises and coppers. They are chosen young for their speed and small unremarkable frames in crowds. They run messages through guarded streets using memorized lantern codes and chalk marks, changing them with the moon. Ordinary folk often mistake these youthful runners for common beggars and pickpockets. In combat they throw sparks and run rather than stand and fight like adults, preferring flight to valor. Their quick legs are useful, but their blades remain unreliable, short, and poorly maintained. They memorize patrol routes carefully, and sweets can purchase useful information from them. A caught genin often cries and reveals everything they know almost immediately. Each captured runner teaches cells to compartmentalize, while younger siblings volunteer eagerly for coin, younger every year. Surviving genin graduate to full operatives within years, and masters invest heavily in the promising ones, watching for talent.
payload.base_appearance: A youthful runner loiters in ragged wraps with signal strips, quick feet, and wide eyes. Small frame, patched clothes, and a message satchel mark an apprentice, visibly under twenty. Restless energy and darting glances promise speed, curiosity, and incomplete training.
payload.portrait_brief: A young round face peers beneath ragged wraps, with bright frightened eyes and scraped chin. Soft cheeks and bitten nails convey youth, hunger, and eagerness to belong.

variants.name: Errand Boy

variants.name: Alley Runner
variants.appearance_delta: A small girl with quiet shoes, chalk marks, and knowledge of patrol bells.

He tosses his spark packet down and flees through legs and market stalls.

payload.display_name: Chunin (older high rank, all mature visuals, higher stats)
payload.body: Chunin lead cells and plan difficult entries after many experienced seasons in the field, commanding shadows and knives. They read guards and weather expertly, timing actions that younger others execute. Employers pay more for their seasoned judgment than for their personal blades, which matter less than judgment. In combat they strike short and hard while directing genin positioned around them. Their steady decisions anchor retreats that might otherwise become panicked flights, saving cells from ruin. Their scars provide lessons that younger operatives cannot easily learn or buy. Age may slow their legs, but never their watchful calculating eyes at night. Losing a chunin can collapse an entire operative cell within a matter of weeks. Each surviving commander trains two successors, while captured ones doom whole networks to arrests, and fill interrogation cells. Dead chunin are mourned in coded toasts, and their cells scatter to new masters within weeks, drinking to fallen planners.
payload.base_appearance: A mature operative commands in quality wraps with a command fan, grey at the temples. Fine bindings, sealed orders, and a weathered map mark rank, visibly above thirty years. A still posture and slow gestures promise judgment worth more than blades.
payload.portrait_brief: A lined composed face studies the plan beneath grey temples, with calm commanding eyes. A trimmed beard and steady mouth convey experience, authority, and concealed ruthlessness.

variants.name: Older Field-Lead

variants.name: Grey Planner

variants.name: Older Handler

variants.name: Grey Coordinator

She sits composed giving orders, captured but still shielding the network's names.

payload.display_name: Teppo Shinobi (matchlock ninja, flagged mundane firearm tech, no new magic)
payload.body: Teppo shinobi shoot from lofts and field blinds using long heavy matchlock tubes and rests, wrapped in oilcloth and secrecy. This late craft was learned from foreign traders, entirely without enchantment or sorcery. Their single roaring shot can decide an ambush before blades ever meet in anger, deciding fates at a hundred paces. Crowds scatter quickly when smoke suddenly blooms around their hidden elevated positions. They rent upper rooms quietly and abandon heavy tubes while fleeing through back alleys. In combat they rely upon one devastating shot before resorting to weak swordplay, for tubes teach no fencing. Rain and damp weather ruin the precious powder they require for reliable firing. Shuttered windows and zigzagging approaches effectively foil their patient preparations and aim. The matchlock itself remains a flagged mundane tech proposal, never final canon under doctrine, pending explicit human approval. Gunsmiths who serve teppo cells grow rich quietly, and foreign traders raise powder prices yearly.
payload.base_appearance: A hooded marksman braces a long tube on a rest-stick, with powder-horn and smoke-stained sleeves. Heavy barrel, measured powder, and padded shoulder mark an unfamiliar foreign-taught craft. A prone stillness behind blinds promises a single decisive roar before flight.
payload.portrait_brief: A powder-smudged wary face squints above a scarf, with a singed brow and ringing ears. Narrowed eyes and a burnt cheek convey novelty, danger, and technical obsession.

variants.name: Young Gunner
variants.appearance_delta: A keen young shot with a new tube, measured powder, and steady hands.

variants.name: Older Shot

variants.name: Keen Gunner

variants.name: Older Loader

He fires with a roaring loose that fills the loft with blinding smoke.
He staggers drawing a weak short sword as guards rush through the smoke.

payload.body: Village militias are farmers and craftspeople mustered with spears and warning bells for defense, answering the old oak bell. They defend barns and homes when thieves threaten nearby families late at night. They drill on rest days beneath retired soldiers' stern and patient instruction in squares. Neighbors trust these familiar defenders more than distant garrison troops from fortresses. In combat they bravely hold hedge lines despite raw and uneven experience with blood, but rich in stubbornness. Heavy rushes can break them, though warning bells rally them quickly to reform. Their strength comes from numbers and intimate knowledge of every inch of home ground, every ditch and stile. At dawn they disperse again to their ordinary daily work in fields and workshops. Each repelled raid strengthens the muster for years, while each defeat teaches harder drill, under sterner sergeants. Mustered villages earn charters and tax relief, and lords prefer cheap militias to costly garrisons.
payload.base_appearance: A homespun defender stands the bell-line in a patched coat, with spear, hide shield, and harvest boots. Work-hardened hands, familiar faces, and mended kit mark neighbors rather than soldiers. A nervous but determined line promises defense of homes, not conquest.
payload.portrait_brief: An earnest weathered face grips a spear beneath a straw hat, with anxious determined eyes. A sunburned nose and set jaw convey fear mastered by neighborly duty.

variants.name: Young Plowman
variants.appearance_delta: A strong young farmer with a new spear, broad shoulders, and harvest strength.

variants.name: Older Headman
variants.appearance_delta: A grey village elder with a tally of service, calm voice, and authority.

variants.name: Hard Wife
variants.appearance_delta: A stout young mother with a pitchfork, fierce eyes, and children behind her.

variants.name: Young Daughter
variants.appearance_delta: A quick girl with a sling, bell-rope, and runner's knowledge of lanes.

state_poses.description: She stands the bell-line with spear braced, shoulder touching her neighbor's shield.
She thrusts with a spear-poke in unison as the bell clangs the warning.

payload.body: Watchmen walk night rounds carrying lanterns and halberds through quiet sleeping market towns, swinging lanterns against the dark. They know familiar drunks and troublesome doors by name, habit, and nightly routine. Folk mock them during calm days, yet miss them sorely afterward when thieves arrive, begging for their return. In combat they stand steady with halberds and call loudly for help early. They hold narrow lanes rather than attempting open battlefield maneuvers against cavalry, which they wisely avoid. Their shrill whistles summon heavier help when trouble exceeds their small numbers. Poor pay leaves some watchmen vulnerable to tempting heavy bribes at quiet gates. Honest watchmen nevertheless keep regular rounds through difficult weather and dark nights. Each kept round deters a burglary for weeks, while missed ones invite gangs within days, and cost captains their posts. Pensioned watchmen become doorkeepers and night guides, and taverns reserve them honored stools, listening for old rounds.
payload.base_appearance: A lantern-halberdier patrols in a town cloak with a whistle-cord and badge-disk gleaming. Swung lantern, grounded halberd, and measured tread mark lawful night authority. A weary circuit and raised lamp promise that someone watches while townsfolk sleep.
payload.portrait_brief: A tired honest face swings a lantern beneath a watch cap, with heavy eyes and lined cheeks. A drooping mustache and patient mouth convey routine, low pay, and stubborn duty.

variants.name: Young Recruit

payload.body: Hedge wardens guard field boundaries and orchards from poachers and hungry night boars, walking bounds in all weathers. They work as solitary trackers carrying short bows through tangled thorny vegetation. Farmers feed them gladly to keep watchful eyes facing outward every night, for bread and cider. In combat they snipe first from deep cover, then fall back with knives drawn. They understand snares better than most formally trained soldiers ever will, giving every inch grudgingly. Their dogs help track intruders and warn of approaching danger well ahead. Long winters thin their regular rounds across exposed and frozen boundary fields. Briar scratches and muddy boots mark their persistent lonely outdoor work. Each caught poacher feeds the village for weeks, while each missed one empties snares nightly, and starves the village pot. Veteran wardens map every sett and snare for their successors, and poachers curse their names for decades, teaching dogs and daughters alike.
payload.base_appearance: A green-cloaked tracker crouches at the hedge in briar-scratched leathers, with a short bow and snares. Mud-caked boots, spare strings, and a quiet dog mark a solitary professional of boundaries. A still patience among thorns promises arrows for poachers before any warning.
payload.portrait_brief: A lean weathered face watches from a hood, with green eyes and briar-scratched cheeks. A quiet mouth and scarred hands convey solitude, tracking, and territorial certainty.

payload.body: Fire brigades are bucket and hook crews who answer sudden fires at the bells, running with hooks and orders. During riots or raids, they double as practical axe militia for the barricaded streets. Masons and roofers fill their ranks, making them strong and steady on tall ladders. Settlements love them after fires but fear their strength during street brawls and riots. In combat they swing axes and hooks with labor-hardened force and practiced teamwork, forged in soot and sweat. Their experience balancing above streets lets them hold rooftops remarkably well under missiles. Brigade bells rally nearby militias whenever immediate reinforcements are urgently needed. Dry seasons keep every crew alert, organized, and ready through hot windless nights. Each quenched fire builds civic pride for years, while each riot reminds towns of their axes, while widows collect the relief fund. Honored brigades parade on founding days with polished axes, and children dream of joining their ranks.
payload.base_appearance: A soot-stained crew braces a ladder with fire-axe, hook-pole, and leather helm gleaming. Blackened coats, rope belts, and bucket lines mark professionals of flame and rescue. Chalked arms and steady footing promise order inside burning chaos.
payload.portrait_brief: A soot-blackened grinning face shouts beneath a leather helm, with red eyes and cracked lips. A singed brow and strong jaw convey courage, labor, and familiarity with flames.

payload.body: River patrols pole narrow skiffs along winding channels checking toll tokens and smugglers, searching mist and reeds. They know hidden reeds, shifting shallows, and reliable crossing places intimately by season. Boatmen either respect their authority or attempt to bribe them quietly at landings. In combat they hook and shove effectively from their unstable rocking boats, with coin and silence. Ashore, their waterborne training leaves them notably weaker than regular opponents with shields, where balance beats strength. They defend waterways diligently, not broad land routes or fortified stone walls. Their narrow skiffs serve as mobile forts among familiar winding reed channels. Strong storms beach patrols and leave waterways temporarily unguarded for bold smugglers. Each seized contraband funds new skiffs, while each accepted bribe rots the patrol from within, though honest crews endure. Drowned patrollers are honored with river funerals, and their hooks hang in toll houses afterward, draped with reeds and honors.
payload.base_appearance: An oilskin patroller poles a narrow skiff in bare feet, with a boat-hook and token-board. Official braid, sealed tallies, and a signal horn mark lawful authority on the water. A balanced stance against the current promises inspection backed by hooks and numbers.

payload.body: Line infantry march and hold with spear and shield for seasonal employers across disputed borders, marching in all weathers. They keep step steadily where less trained militias bunch together in fear and confusion. Villagers respect their solid line when it blocks narrow passes against raiders and deserters. In combat they are steady wall-fighters, pushing forward slowly and reluctant to rout. They advance together to the measured beat of military drums and sergeants' shouts, grinding forward like mills. Their strength comes from the shoulders of neighboring soldiers standing in line. Broken lines rarely reform once fear separates their frightened and scattered members, once panic takes hold. Officers place them where a dependable wall matters most in the coming battle. Each held pass builds their legend for years, while each rout teaches harder drill and discipline, under louder sergeants. Discharged infantry become guards and caravan muscle, and their drill never quite leaves them, even in taverns.
payload.base_appearance: A uniform-coated spearman advances in step with shield, marching pack, and leveled spear. Matching coats, hobnailed boots, and regimental badges mark drilled professionals of the line. Ranked shoulders and synchronized tread promise a wall that advances without breaking.

payload.body: Crossbowmen loose heavy bolts from behind lines, often recruited from experienced hunter stock, spanning steel at dawn. They need little training to kill effectively at distance from behind tall pavises. Defenders on walls fear the force of their concentrated and disciplined volleys, darkening the noon sky. In combat they shoot in volleys, then brace behind pavises with short swords ready. Alone and unsupported, they are weak once enemies close into furious melee, where pavises become coffins. They reload beneath cover while armored comrades hold the line ahead of them. Wet strings slow their work and make each shot uncertain, short, wild, and wasted. Their heavy bolts can pierce mail at useful battlefield range through gaps. Each volley decides engagements early, while heavy rain renders them helpless spectators behind shields, cursing the clouds. Spanning crossbowmen develop massive shoulders and calm nerves, and surgeons envy their steady hands, recruiting them for delicate work.
payload.base_appearance: A pavise-bearer kneels behind a tall shield with a crossbow, bolt-case, and padded jack. Cranequin, spare strings, and stacked bolts mark a professional of prepared volleys. A sheltered rhythm of span, load, and loose promises disciplined distant killing.

payload.body: Scout riders range ahead on hardy ponies, carrying sharp eyes and brass warning horns, far beyond all support. They count enemy camps and burn fodder before larger columns arrive in force. Marching columns depend heavily upon their timely warnings and accurate route reports, drawn in charcoal and memory. In combat they skirmish with javelins and never stand fast against heavy charges. They flee dangerous encounters in order to deliver critical reports intact and swiftly, living to report another day. Their hardy mountain ponies outlast the heavier mounts of armored chargers. Hunger and lameness can ground even the most skilled and willing rider for weeks. A warning horn lets distant allies prepare for discovered danger in good time. Each accurate report saves columns from ambush, while each missed patrol invites disaster and slaughter, and ends officers' careers. Famous scouts retire as guides and horse breeders, and armies pay dearly for their maps, marking every ford.
payload.base_appearance: A light horseman circles at distance in a dust-cloak, with javelins, horn, and a hardy pony. Light saddle, spare shoes, and far-seeing eyes mark a professional of vanguard and warning. A loose rein and constant scanning promise intelligence delivered before battle begins.

payload.body: Sappers dig, bridge, and break obstacles using mattocks and mundane black-powder kegs under fire, steadily toward victory. Many come from mining families accustomed to dangerous underground labor and bad air. Forts dread the tunnels and mines these quiet workers prepare beneath proud walls. In combat they blast gates first with powder, then fight on with picks and shovels. They are clumsy fighters when caught across open level ground without cover, where picks move slowly. They work beneath shields while comrades protect them from falling missiles and sorties. Their powder kegs are precious cargo guarded jealously during every march and camp, sleeping beside the fuses. Floodwater can drown their mines before a planned breach ever succeeds at dawn. Each breached wall justifies their wages for years, while each flooded mine teaches better drainage, while engineers plan drier galleries. Master sappers consult for fortresses across the continent, and kings ransom captured engineers rather than hang them.
payload.base_appearance: A dirt-caked digger crouches with a pick, powder-keg, and timber props in a muddy apron. Fuse coils, shovels, and reinforced boots mark a professional of tunnels and breaches. A low stance and careful hands promise walls undermined before dawn assaults.

payload.body: Standard bearers carry bright colors that hold fighting lines together through steady visible presence, shining above the smoke. They rarely strike blows themselves, yet whole armies can break when they fall. New recruits watch their cloth for signs of ordered movement amid chaos and smoke, watching for the cloth. In combat they defend with short swords while lifting heavy poles high overhead. Nearby allies rally around the raised colors during confusion and bloody retreat, eyes fixed on the pole. Their loss spreads panic through troops who cannot see direction or orders anymore. Guards surround them whenever battle grows especially close and dangerous to commanders. Their cloth is carefully mended after every hard campaign by grateful regimental hands. Each held color saves regiments from rout, while each fallen one scatters veterans like raw recruits, to every commander's horror. Fallen colors are avenged by entire regiments, and recovered banners earn medals for the retrievers, parading them through cheering towns.
payload.base_appearance: A tall bearer stands colors-high in braided cords, with a pole, short sword, and steady arms. Embroidered cloth, polished finial, and guarded stance mark the army's visible soul. An upright planted posture promises direction amid smoke, noise, and fear.

payload.body: Hedge knights wander between hire and tourney with dented harness and one faithful horse, and dented empty saddlebags. They own no land at all, possessing only arms, armor, and their loyal mount. Villagers hire them against dangerous brutes they cannot face alone with pitchforks, paying in grain and gratitude. In combat they are solid mounted fighters with lance, sword, and battered shield. They pride themselves on thundering charges but become brittle in deep sucking mud, where glory drowns quickly. They keep old vows of protection whenever an employer pays fairly and feeds them. Their horses eat generously before their riders accept any meal themselves at inns. A lame horse can quickly reduce a proud hedge knight to walking poverty. Each rescued village feeds legends for decades, while each dead horse ends a career, leaving ballads unfinished. Ballads remember generous hedge knights for centuries, and village children bear their names with pride, singing of rescues.
payload.base_appearance: A dented rider salutes in patched barding with a lance, arming sword, and weathered shield. Scarred harness, mended straps, and a lean horse mark nobility without lands. A straight seat and battered crest promise honor maintained on empty purses.

payload.body: Household knights guard manors and caravans for steady board and reliable monthly pay, eating at the high table's foot. They are better fed than hedge kin who wander between uncertain and distant employers. They drill courtyard youths in the basics of weapons and discipline every morning, before the household wakes. Households trust their gates and family members to these familiar sworn knights. In combat they hold doors with disciplined sword and shield work for hours, unyielding as oak doors. They retreat alongside their charges rather than leaving them exposed to assassins. Their livery is plain cloth displaying no named heraldry or house symbols at all. Their service remains personal, built on familiar daily responsibility and mutual trust. Each protected household renews their oath yearly, while dismissed ones wander as hedge blades, poorer but freer. Pensioned household knights train pages and guard chapels, and great houses honor them at feasts, seating them near the hearth.
payload.base_appearance: A clean man-at-arms guards the door in a blank household cloak, with sword, shield, and polished boots. Maintained harness, trimmed tabard, and steady drill mark a professional of gates and corridors. A planted doorway stance promises that nothing passes without permission or blood.
payload.portrait_brief: A loyal composed face watches the corridor beneath a plain helm, with steady devoted eyes. A clean jaw and trimmed hair convey service, discipline, and household pride.

payload.body: Squires are youthful apprentice fighters tending horses and harness while learning arms daily, mucking stalls before dawn. Chosen for promise, they polish equipment, carry supplies, and keep night watch faithfully. Households feed them generously because they expect future capable blades in return, worth every loaf and lesson. In combat they are eager but half-trained with sword and buckler against veterans. They rush beyond their skill whenever a knight requires urgent protection in battle, outrunning their own fear. They guard knights' backs fiercely despite their incomplete training and small size. Their mistakes teach them faster than careful instruction ever could in safety, though scars last longest. Veterans eventually shape them into fighters or break their confidence entirely. Each surviving squire earns spurs or scars, while broken ones return quietly to stables, wiser and humbler. Knighted squires remember their training years fondly, and sponsor poor pages in their turn, endowing stables and schools, funding scholarships for stable brats.
payload.base_appearance: A youthful attendant-fighter stands eager with a borrowed sword, buckler, and horse-brush at the belt. Polished harness, feed sacks, and a too-large helm mark apprenticeship, visibly young. Bright readiness and quick obedience promise future knights learning through service.

payload.body: Foot knights fight dismounted in full harness with poleaxes at gates and smoking breaches, planted like iron statues. Their heavy equipment makes long marches and marshes especially difficult and dangerously slow. Forts prize them as defenders wherever walls face direct assault by sappers, daring them to dig. In combat they are crushing close fighters but painfully slow to turn. They hold breaches against foes who attempt to force entry with rams, breaking like waves on rock. Their harness needs squires for fitting, repair, and daily oiling care. Mud can fell them before their weapons ever reach determined opponents, floundering helpless in mire. They prefer firm ground where their armor's weight becomes true protection. Each held breach saves garrisons for years, while each fallen knight must be winched upright, to the squires' despair. Dented foot knights guard bridges and gates into old age, and young soldiers marvel at their scars, asking for the old stories.
payload.base_appearance: A full-harness fighter braces the gate-stand with a poleaxe and plain crested helm. Plate, padding, and a lowered visor mark a walking fortress of jointed steel. Planted weight and leveled axe promise that breaches will cost attackers dearly.

payload.body: Tourney champions live for prize bouts in fair towns and fleeting seasonal fame, chasing purses and applause. Crowds chant for nameless favors when they unhorse celebrated rivals in the lists. They hire themselves as duelists during the intervals between great summer fairs, fighting for supper money. In combat they use showy precision with lance and sword together to dazzle. They seek dramatic falls rather than killing defeated opponents outright before crowds, preserving drama and purses. They challenge travelers to contests at mounted passes along busy trade roads. Their prizes pay for armor, horses, and lavish public display throughout winter, seeking reckless challengers. A lost bout can empty purses and damage their reputation for entire seasons. Each victory brings richer patrons and better horses, while each defeat sends them to lesser fairs, with dented armor. Aged champions judge lists and train heirs, and their trophies gather dust in honored halls, telling taller tales yearly.
payload.base_appearance: A bright-harness rider circles in polished steel with a ribboned lance and gleaming helm. Silks, favors, and a groomed destrier mark a professional of spectacle and prize money. A theatrical seat and lifted lance promise entertainment backed by genuine skill.
payload.portrait_brief: A handsome confident face smiles beneath a polished helm, with bright teeth and vain eyes. A groomed jaw and oiled hair convey fame, pride, and practiced showmanship.

payload.body: Oathswords swear personal solemn vows to protect travelers and sick people along lonely dangerous roads, asking nothing but bread. They carry plain unadorned swords and ask no payment from temples or grateful poor villages. Folk offer bread for blessings these humble mortal fighters cannot truly give or guarantee. They walk dark roads deliberately where ordinary guards are few, corrupt, or entirely absent. In combat they are steady sword-and-shield fighters standing over the fallen and shielding them, unmoving as chapel stones. They never claim spells or miracles, relying only upon steadfast arms and tested courage. Their oaths forbid flight whenever helpless people need their protection against brigands. Broken oaths exile them from the trust of ordinary folk forever and everywhere. Any oath-blessing capacity remains a flagged holy proposal under magic doctrine, never final canon law, pending explicit human approval. Fallen oathswords are buried where they stood, and travelers leave stones upon their cairns.

payload.display_name: Chapel Guard (fighters + warding prayers, holy flagged proposal)
payload.body: Chapel guards watch small shrines and burial grounds faithfully without claiming priesthood or sanctity, only brooms and keys. They sweep steps daily and turn away thieves seeking easy offerings and altar silver. Mourners trust their quiet presence during difficult ceremonies and lonely midnight visits, weeping among the stones. In combat they fight with mace and lantern-shield at narrow consecrated gates. They hold thresholds stubbornly rather than follow enemies onto open bloody battlefields, which cowards wisely shun. Their duty ends at the walls surrounding their consecrated and beloved charge. Their keys rattle whenever they make a careful nightly round through fog. Thieves learn that quiet shrines may still have determined and wakeful defenders. Any warding-prayer capacity remains a flagged holy proposal under magic doctrine, never final canon law, pending explicit human approval and review. Long-serving chapel guards are buried in the yards they kept, and mourners tend their graves, leaving lanterns burning.
payload.base_appearance: A grey-robed guard holds the gate-stand with a mace, lantern-shield, and heavy key-ring. Swept steps, trimmed wicks, and a watchful round mark humble sacred custodianship. A planted threshold stance promises that desecration will be paid for dearly.
payload.portrait_brief: A calm watchful face glows beside a lantern beneath a grey hood, with patient eyes. A smooth brow and quiet mouth convey reverence, routine, and unshowy courage.

payload.display_name: Mendicant Protector (fighters + mendicant blessings, holy flagged proposal)
payload.body: Mendicant protectors walk with begging healers, carrying staves against wolves and roadside thieves, barefoot and utterly fearless. They own nothing except bowls, patched robes, and necessary walking tools for the road. Villagers feed the pair whenever their charity can spare food, shelter, and bandages, given gladly by the poor. In combat they whirl staves to shield unarmed companions without killing their attackers. They retreat alongside their charges when stronger enemies press forward in numbers, turning blades aside gently. Their vows forbid loot taken from defeated foes or helpless frightened travelers. Their bare feet mark long journeys across rough roads and stony mountain passes. They depend upon mobility and goodwill instead of expensive armor and warhorses. Any mendicant-blessing capacity remains a flagged holy proposal under magic doctrine, never final canon law, pending explicit human approval and review. Beloved mendicants are fed in every village they pass, and children follow their staffs for miles, begging blessings.
payload.base_appearance: A barefoot staff-fighter circles protectively in a patched robe, with a bowl strapped at the back. Calloused feet, worn staff, and an alms bowl mark poverty chosen as discipline. A mobile guard stance promises that healers will never stand alone.
payload.portrait_brief: A gentle weathered face smiles beneath a shaven head, with kind eyes and cracked lips. A calm brow and dusty cheeks convey charity, walking, and unarmed courage.

payload.display_name: Relic Warden (fighters + relic-ward prayers, holy flagged proposal)
payload.body: Relic wardens escort carts carrying old bones and banners reverently between quiet rural hamlets, singing hymns on the march. They claim no power within relics, only a humble duty of watchful care. Crowds follow the cart when it travels for seasonal festivals, funerals, and blessings, growing at every crossroads. In combat they defend the wagon with halberds without advancing a single step. Their loss scatters pilgrims who depended upon their visible and trusted protection, rooted like gateposts. Their carts are plain wood, built for travel rather than rich display or comfort. Thieves repeatedly test whether the wardens can defend valuable cargo at night, testing locks and nerves. Wardens keep close watch on every chest, wheel, axle, and harness strap. Any relic-ward prayer capacity remains a flagged holy proposal under magic doctrine, never final canon law. Faithful relic wardens walk entire provinces in a lifetime, and festival crowds remember their steady pace.
payload.base_appearance: A cart-guard walks the wagon-side with a halberd, relic-chest key, and festival ribbons. Plain harness, sealed chests, and a steady pace mark reverent transport duty. A close escort stance promises that the cart will reach its shrine intact.

payload.display_name: Penitent Blade (fighters + penitent zeal, holy flagged proposal)
payload.body: Penitent blades are former criminals working through guilt by serving the victims they wronged, without wages or rest. They wear ropes at their waists as visible signs of lasting and public remorse. Folk distrust them first, then praise those who prove steadfast over many seasons, earning slow grudging trust. In combat they fight fiercely with flails and seek holy wounds as payment. They spare surrendering foes because mercy demonstrates changed intentions better than words, sparing even the cruel. Their past deeds continue to drive every difficult choice they make on roads. Formal pardons release most from their chosen lifelong service eventually and mercifully. Some remain in service because forgiveness never quiets their guilt at night. Any penitent zeal capacity remains a flagged holy proposal under magic doctrine, never final canon law, pending explicit human approval. Forgiven penitents sometimes found hostels for the guilty, and their ropes hang in chapels afterward, as warnings and hope.
payload.base_appearance: A rope-bound fighter advances bowed in a plain shirt, with a flail, scarred face, and bare feet. Hemp rope, self-made scars, and a dented flail mark guilt carried as armor. A lowered head and raised weapon promise that punishment will be shared forward.

payload.body: Palace sentries stand at inner doors of great households, chosen for absolute stillness and memory, still as carved stone. They memorize familiar faces, footsteps, and the rhythms of daily visitors and servants. Residents ignore them completely until an alarm makes their vigilance suddenly necessary, transforming statues into steel. In combat they hold doorways with spears and shout warnings before striking intruders. They never pursue intruders beyond the posts assigned to them by standing orders, never chasing glory or coin. Their shifts are long, demanding focus during the quietest and darkest hours. Bribes test their loyalty almost every night of their otherwise uneventful service. A sentry who recognizes danger quickly can protect an entire sleeping household. Each foiled intrusion raises their standing for years, while each slept watch ends careers in disgrace, and feeds corridor gossip. Decorated sentries earn posts by royal doors, and their stillness becomes legend among the guards, recounted to recruits.
payload.base_appearance: A motionless spearman holds the door-post in a plain unmarked household cloak, spear vertical. Polished boots, steady breathing, and an empty gaze mark a professional of stillness. An unmoving planted stance promises that the threshold itself has come alive.
payload.portrait_brief: An impassive watchful face stares past visitors, with level eyes and a closed mouth. A smooth brow and disciplined stillness convey patience, memory, and incorruptible routine.

payload.body: Escort lancers ride beside carriages on open roads with bright leveled lances and pennants, gleaming in polished pairs. They drill in pairs to coordinate charges and shifting protective screens around coaches. Travelers pay extra for the safety their visible pennants and armor promise, gladly emptying heavy purses. In combat they charge to scatter ambushes before screening orderly retreats to safety. They abandon baggage when necessary to save people placed under their protection, shielding screaming noble passengers. Their horses are better fed than nearly every other mount on the roads. Lameness grounds a lancer and removes their chief advantage entirely in an instant. A paired charge can open space for a carriage escape through closing brigands. Each safe arrival earns generous bonuses, while each lost carriage ends contracts and reputations, ending even old friendships. Famous escorts command premium rates and choose their own clients, and merchants bid for their pennants, season after season.

payload.body: Vault wardens guard strong-rooms and granaries of great households using heavy paired keys, jingling with every step. They count seals nightly and record any irregularity immediately in bound ledgers. Stewards trust their tallies because stock losses threaten everyone nearby with hunger, from lord to scullion. In combat they fight with short swords among tightly packed chests and barrels. They never leave the rooms placed under their direct sworn protection for any reason, counting exits between strokes. They may flood or burn stores rather than yield them intact to besiegers. Their duplicate keys hang separately to prevent one easy theft from opening vaults. Torture threatens them whenever intruders seek access to protected stores at night. Each balanced tally extends their tenure for years, while each missing seal ends it swiftly, and blacklists the family. Retired vault wardens audit great houses for fees, and stewards compete to hire their eyes, paying in gold and secrets.
payload.base_appearance: A key-hung guard leans watchful among chests with a short sword, seal-board, and iron-shod boots. Ringed keys, wax tallies, and a barred door mark a professional of stores and vaults. A close miserly stance promises that nothing leaves without tally and permission.

payload.body: Honor blades duel challengers who insult their households under strict formal counts and witnesses, bowing to seconds and surgeons. They practice daily to maintain exact timing and careful elegant footwork in the salle. Their scars are displayed proudly as evidence of past public contests and victories. In combat they are precise sword duelists seeking disarms before wounds and deaths. They refuse group brawls that make honorable counts impossible to keep or judge, so they sheath steel and walk away. Their seconds watch closely for broken rules or unfair interference from the crowd. Lost duels bring shame upon the households they proudly represent before peers. They value measured skill over the chaos of muddy battlefield fighting and brawling. Each victorious duel burnishes the household name for seasons, while each defeat demands rematch or apology, under the code's harsh eye. Aged honor blades referee duels and teach the code, and their word settles disputes finally, without appeal.
payload.base_appearance: A slim duelist salutes in polished boots with a plain sword and a second's sash. Measured stance, clean blade, and a formal sash mark a professional of counted honor. A poised stillness promises that insults will be answered under strict rules.
payload.portrait_brief: A cool composed face regards the challenger over a leveled blade, with distant proud eyes. A thin scar and pressed collar convey practice, pride, and formal restraint.

payload.body: Night watch captains command household guards after dark, checking posts with hooded lanterns, silent in slippered feet. They know every corridor creak and each guard's expected position entirely by heart. Sleeping residents trust their careful rounds to reveal any hidden threat before dawn, reading shadows and whispers. In combat they direct guards with whistles and halberds on narrow stairs. They rally sentries quickly when an alarm breaks ordinary night routine and silence, summoning every drowsy spear. Their books log every entry, departure, and unexpected disturbance faithfully each night. Missed rounds can doom them when a breach follows unnoticed in darkness. Lantern light and disciplined patrols make their authority visible and deeply reassuring. Each quiet night extends their command for years, while each breach ends it in disgrace, by cold accusing torchlight. Retired night captains sleep through their first dawns in years, and daylight astonishes their tired eyes, dreaming of rounds and bells.
payload.base_appearance: A lantern-captain holds the stair-stand with a halberd, whistle, and round-book at the belt. Oiled cloak, checked posts, and a steady lamp mark command of sleeping households. A mobile watchful circuit promises that no corridor goes unwatched until dawn.
payload.portrait_brief: A stern wakeful face peers past the lantern glow, with tired commanding eyes and lined cheeks. A trimmed beard and heavy brow convey vigilance, records, and nocturnal authority.
